title: sprint-harness configuration
description: The single file that makes the harness portable. Everything project-specific that core/ needs lives here; nothing project-specific lives in core/.

worktree.description: Basename of the directory sprints MUST run from. null disables the check. Set it when the repo has more than one worktree and only one of them is publishable.

map.description: The knowledge base the queue is derived from. Optional: a project can hand-maintain QUEUE.json and skip the map entirely.

requireCommitted.description: Builders run in git worktrees, which materialize only TRACKED files. An uncommitted map is invisible to every builder while you are reading the new one.

checkCmd.description: Optional command that exits non-zero when a derived artifact (an HTML render, an index) is stale.

writeOnlyFrom.description: Worktree basename allowed to run the extractor with --write. File citations resolve against the working tree, so writing the queue from a different worktree can silently produce a different collision graph.

anchors.description: The exit codes this harness trusts. NOT a style preference — an anchor is a command a builder runs and an independent verifier RE-RUNS. A disagreement between the two is the single most valuable signal the system produces.

id.description: Short identifier. Becomes a key in the builder/verifier structured output, so keep it a bare word.

whenTouches.description: Run this anchor only when the diff touches one of these paths/prefixes. Keeps a slow anchor off nodes that cannot have broken it.

setup.description: Commands every builder and verifier runs BEFORE the anchors, in a fresh worktree.

why.description: Shown verbatim in the agent contracts. Say what breaks if the agent improvises a shortcut — agents skip steps whose cost they cannot see.

lanes.description: Categories of work that CANNOT be parallelised against each other, regardless of which files they touch. The canonical case is numbered forward-only migrations: two agents cannot both mint the next number, and no merge can resolve it.

itemFlag.description: Boolean field on a queue item. Every selected item with this flag truthy is unioned into one serial node.

pairedArtifacts.description: Mechanical 'if you changed X you must also change Y' gates, with an auditable waiver. This exists because the same rule as PROSE in an agent contract produced three test files across fifty-one components.

pairPath.description: Template for the required counterpart. {name} = source basename without extension. e.g. "web/components/__tests__/{name}.test.tsx"

waiverTrailer.description: Commit-message trailer that waives the rule for ONE named source file. Blanket waivers are unsupported on purpose — an exemption must be greppable and arguable.

help.description: Printed on failure. Point at the pattern to copy.

lenses.description: One verifier per lens per node, each with a context that has never seen the builder's. Distinct QUESTIONS, not redundant reviewers — which is why ONE reject fails a node rather than being outvoted.

requireAllLenses.description: A node is accepted only when every lens actually returned. A lens that crashed leaves the node UNVERIFIED, which is not the same outcome as rejected.

denyPushReason.description: Shown to the agent on denial. State what the real gate is, so the agent stops instead of hunting for another route.

stackBranches.description: When true, preflight refuses to call the main branch a valid base while ANY local branch is ahead of the remote. Branching from main there silently drops every unpushed commit from your base.

excludeFromStacking.description: Branches that are permanently ahead of the remote by design (a demo branch, a never-pushed integration branch) and are therefore not stacking bases.

marker.description: String that must appear in .git/hooks/pre-push for preflight to consider the guard installed.
